Priyom / Irene / Samantha — quick triage from the runtime side:

Observations (first-pass):
- We see a noisy-neighbor pattern on the physical node subset that backs LambdaPay's dedicated pool. One tenant's KV cache backlog is causing disproportionate GPU mem pressure and preventing efficient KV cache reuse.
- Inference scheduling is stalling at the conveyor stage (queue depth up 4x) which leads to token-level serialization and >1.8s tail.
- Error spike correlates with short OOM/retry cycles in one host; not a model bug.

Immediate mitigations proposed (we can execute within 10–20m if approved):
1) Authorize emergency burst + spin up 2 GPU instances from the burst pool to offload hot slices (will reduce token queueing).
2) Apply a temporary routing rule that shifts ~25% of traffic to a slightly smaller quantized model variant (compatible with your quality bar).
3) Drain the noisy tenant from the affected host and rebalance shards (this takes longer; infra scheduling).

I attached a short triage note with observed host ids and logs: triage_notes.pdf (redacted).

Estimate: burst + routing change should regain acceptable latency in ~12–18 minutes; full rebalancing 2–4 hours.

David Kim
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
